newsitem.title: USA: US Northeast spot power pressured by unit startups.
newsitem.headline: US Northeast spot power pressured by unit startups.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. were pressured by Friday by startups of a couple of nuclear stations in the region, marketers said.

Bearish sentiments from more generation back in service were offset by concerns over high fuel costs and the planned outage of two segements of a 765 kilovolt (KV) transmission line from Quebec to New York, marketers said.

The nuclear plants--1,137 megawatt (MW) Nine Mile Point Point nuclear unit 2 in Scriba, N.Y. and 510 MW Vermont Yankee nuclear plant in Vernon, Vt.,--were expected to resume full output by next week from refueling shutdowns.

The New York Power Authority (NYPA) said it will shut, beginning today, two portions of a 765 kilovolt (KV) transmission line that runs between Quebec and central New York for seasonal maintenance. The entire line has a capacity of 2,350 megawatts (MW) of electricity. The two segments were expected to return to service November 8.

In the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) district, peak, non-firm electricity for Monday was assessed at $24.00-$25.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), flat from Thursday's prices for Friday delivery.
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during light load hours on Monday again stayed in the $14.00-$15.00 range.
In the eastern part of NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for Monday delivery was pegged at $29.00-$31.00, down from Thursday's quote $34.00-$35.00.
Off-peak, non-firm Monday electricity in eastern NYPP was held steady near $17.00.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Monday at the Northeast Utilities border was discussed at $33.00-$35.00, down from Thursday's range of $36.25-$37.25 for Friday.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Monday delivery to the NU border was quoted at $20.00-$21.00, flat from Thursday's quote for Friday delivery.
"On the assumption that Vermont Yankee is coming back, there may be some more room to fall...but not by that much," a Northeast trader, referring to NEPOOL prices.
